reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too crowded!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I honestly do not understand all the 5 star reviews.   This place feels like a cheesy Club Med filled with lots of tourists on a beach that is way too small to comfortably accommodate the numbers of people that unload off these tour boats.  Once you arrive you are asked to pay a minimum of 100 baht to use the toilets and get a chair.  The chairs are flimsy plastic and arranged like they are in a movie theater instead of spaced for relaxing on the beach.  But that is because the beach is not big enough for that kind of spacing.  If you like crowds and being jammed in with others then you might like this.  We did get a drink and food to try to make the most of it as we paid for a private boat to take us.  Food was very mediocre and overpriced for what it was.  My husband and I were horrified and couldn’t wait to get away.  Honestly it was horrifying.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bandya Mama -  Relatively untouched by human interference.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A trip to Banana Beach is incomplete without taking a Banana Boat ride. You will feel a different kind of energy as you will be taken into deep waters through a boat that looks like a banana. These boats are long tubes filled with air that can carry 6 to 8 people. There will be handles on both sides for you to hold on to to avoid falling off. You will also be wearing life jackets that will keep you afloat in case you fall in the water. Exhilarate in a bouncy ride as a speed boat passes your boat, causing turmoil in the water. A thrilling activity that you indulge in at Banana Beach is underwater Sea Walking. You will need to get yourself trained before you can embark on this unique adventure activity.

There are no deck chairs and umbrellas but you shelter from the sun only under the trees. Lots of longtails that take you from the larger nearby beaches like surin and Kamala. Two restaurants on opposite sides with Thai food and more expensive prices than usual. A day here is really recommended

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful guided experience to Banana Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had fun on the day drip to Banana Beach.... Of you are looking for a more 'chill' option over the crowds of Phi Phi, this could be a good choice for you.  We opted for a massage and snorkeling with our package, but other options include parasailing, sea walking, and banana boat (sadly, it was too windy for the boats, but there were a few parasailing slots later in the day when the dind died down).Negatives: The food (buffet included in the tour package) was mediocre (but it's a tiny island and there is only really 1 option). Also during the snorkeling excursion we were surprisingly swarmed by jellyfish( not a problem from the tour operation, just bad luck) but the staff took care of the stings and had vinegar on hand.  Just be mindful if they are close by, as the tide can change and bring them in. Trust me, they definitely sting!  Overall I'd totally recommend this to anyone for a quick 15 min ride from RaoWai.  It feels like a 100 km away, even though you are close by.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nope. Not worth it.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We booked a "Half-day" trip to Banana Beach through our hotel (one of the Wyndham collection).  It was billed as "TUI Destination Experiences." It included pick-up and drop-off at the hotel, lunch buffet, and a speedboat to Banana Beach. We chose a package that included snorkeling in two places and use of a clear kayak. We were to return at 2:00 PM.Once we had booked and paid, the "half-day" tour suddenly became longer than any full-day tours we booked the entire time in Thailand. We were picked up from our hotel at 6:30 AM, and picked up a few other participants at other hotels on the way to the pier.  We were first to be picked up but last dropped off--we did not get back to our hotel until 3:50 PM.  Once at the pier, we waited well over an hour for the boat out to the beach.  We were still sitting on the beach waiting for a boat back when the 2:00 PM return time came and went. Once at Banana Beach, all boats use the single, very long "floating pier." That means that the pier moves violently with the waves, and the water was very choppy.  Walking down the pier was like being on an obstacle course TV show.  It was extremely unsafe.  Even one of the staff working on the pier fell. The beach itself is nice until you take the crowds into consideration.  It ended up being unpleasant, and we just wanted to go back to our hotel.Due to the sea conditions (solely due to light winds), the snorkeling was delayed ("wait until we make a decision at this time," then "wait until we make a decision at this next time") and we were eventually taken to one snorkeling spot, not two. The snorkeling itself was great.  The rest of the trip was not.  The beach was immediately unpleasant, even early in the day, because the tour company allowed clearly intoxicated people on the trip and never addressed their behavior.  They were yelling, playing loud music, and taking video of themselves and everyone else to post to a YouTube channel.  Our group was told we had to stay within one small area of beach chairs, so we were trapped with the drunk/high partiers.  The rest of the beach became quite crowded as the morning went on. Some people decided to use the kayaks, which were offered very late in the day for about 20 minutes of use, and the rest of us were forced to wait for them to finish paddling around a very small and crowded area just off the beach.  We were effectively held hostage.  People who had arrived on other tours were waiting as well, since they were apparently in similar situations.  All of us were unhappy with our "tours." The entirety of Banana Beach seems to be run by one company.  Do not book a group tour of this island/beach if you have anything else planned for that day.  There is no guarantee that you will be returned to the pier in time to catch a flight or even a dinner reservation.  If a bit of a windy but very sunny day causes this much chaos, we cannot imagine what would happen if it rained.  People book tours with set start and end times in mind.  Companies should not be allowed to hold people hostage on an island past the set departure time.

reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spur of the moment trip!My boyfriend and I have 3 days left in Thailand and we decided to go and see one last island for a final day relaxing and swimming before heading back to NZ. This was by far the best experience that we have had on our 2 week trip. The boat was immaculate, the crew were friendly and very informative. Other tours will pack you shoulder to shoulder with strangers and really rush through things. This one does not. The catamaran in 2 levels and there is heaps of space between groups. Parasailing was great and the clear kayaks were in great Knick. Food was not your normal your lunch. It was a sampling menu of some amazing Thai food; prawns, seafood Tom Yum, grilled chicken, papaya salad and super fluffy rice. A la Carte menu is great too. Cocktail buckets are great value. There are small stores in the island and massages available it wanted. This is an awesome way to spend a day. Highly recommend.

We then went further on and stopped to paddle board, snorkel and kayak and they put out the slide to play on. We were then given fresh fruit and cakes (the banana bread was amazing) before setting off to banana island. I would definitely recommend booking the clear kayak at the beach, what an experience! I would book this again in a heartbeat, the staff are lovely and they are helpful to make sure you get everything you might want.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Banana Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Been here yesterday, we have taken the the Program B (Half Day with 1 Activity Included). When we arrived to the check in area, we got a warm Welcome by the Staffs especially Lily. They are providing light breakfast, some breads, fruits, coffee & tea, etc.. We got introduced by the program and explained what we are going to do. We departed at 10am, took a speedboat and reached Banana Beach for 15minutes.Banana Beach is a small island, with clear sea water, white sand, tall trees, it was overall clean. Staffs were excellent in maintaining it clean and of course the service they are providing are beyond magnificent. They also have sun beds which you could use the whole duration of your trip. The company provides different activities such as ZipLine, Banana Boat, Parasailing, Giant Swing, Scuba Diving, Snorkeling, Kayaking (these are all I remember). We originally planned to take the parasailing but due to the strong winds we were unable to do it instead we have done the zip line which has 11 plat forms. After doing the activity, they have served our lunch (fried rice with chicken), also a small bottled water is provided, unlimited!It’s a great place to visit! Hearing the sounds of waves makes you forgot the stressful life in the city.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Banana Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great tour, timetable was planned very efficiently. We booked an all day tour to banana beach in Koh Hey that included a really delicious lunch, snorkeling, and clear bottom kayaking. It was quite crowded on the beach and dining area but not in the ocean. Lots of tourists, but likely due to Lunar New Year holiday for China. The facilities are clean and spaced out. The water is super clear and pristine, lots of areas with coral and fish. The only feedback is probably to have their organization strongly suggest using coral-safe sunblock to the tourists. There was an alarmingly large area of just dead coral on the opposite side of the island where they took us snorkeling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous island with good snorkelling a short boat ride from Phuket
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Trips to Banana Beach are either via the tour company that has exclusive tour access, or via a private speed boat / long tail boat. We visited using the tour company, who also included some snorkelling at a nearby bay, banquet lunch at the Hornbill restaurant, tea/coffee with biscuits for afternoon tea, masks and snorkels, and free water/soft-drink during the day. They also ensured that a gluten-free lunch was available. It was a great day, and the swimming and snorkelling was fantastic. Most of the visitors didn't seem to do this, and instead sat on chairs on the beach, so missed out. The best snorkelling on Banana Beach was on the far side of the pontoon jetty, away from the boats, and there was plenty of coral and fish to see. One of our snorkels was broken, but it was easily swapped over at the hire place, although I suspect it was immediately hired out again, so I suggest checking any masks/snorkels as soon as you hire them.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Such a wonderful day. We loved it.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We booked the Banana Beach tour on a whim with our hotel tour desk at the Diamond Cliff Resort, and this was the best decision we've made since arriving here!We originally booked for the next day, however, I fell ill and couldn't make it. Even though there was a no refund policy after acertain period (6pm night before), upon calling the team early morning when we were supposed to go, they were  accommodating and were able to transfer our booking for the following day.The team were fantastic, friendly, informative and could communicate in perfect English. We had a driver in a shuttle that was air-conditioned pick us up at 8:30 am and take us to the pier. Our guides Lily and Boat were fantastic and spoke great English. The speedboat itself was modern and extremely clean. Our first stop was at Racha Yai Island where we were able to swim or relax on the beach, followed by snorkelling in the coral islands and finally r&r at the beautiful Banana Beach for 3 hours, where we could snorkle, swim and kayak. We chose the clear kayak boat (as part of our full day tour) during decent tide on the day (1pm)and it was stunning to be able to see coral and aquatic life in the clear water. We had a delicious banquet for lunch (which on the day included tom yum soup, satay prawns, sweet chilli calamari, papaya salad, fried chicken and tropical fruits).Extremely glad my husband and I booked this tour on a whim. Loved it!

reviewsWithKeywords.text: Day started very rainy, but our guide, Dream, + her team got us out to Racha Yai, where the sun broke through + we were able to enjoy some snorkeling + time on the beach.  Then we got to Banana Beach, where we were welcomed with a delicious lunch, towels/chairs/activities, and some coffee/tea for the ride home.  Would highly recommend (esp if you’d prefer to stay a little closer to Patong)!

Once you arrive you are asked to pay a minimum of 100 baht to use the toilets and get a chair.  The chairs are flimsy plastic and arranged like they are in a movie theater instead of spaced for relaxing on the beach.  But that is because the beach is not big enough for that kind of spacing.  If you like crowds and being jammed in with others then you might like this.  We did get a drink and food to try to make the most of it as we paid for a private boat to take us. reviews.text: A trip to Banana Beach is incomplete without taking a Banana Boat ride. You will feel a different kind of energy as you will be taken into deep waters through a boat that looks like a banana. These boats are long tubes filled with air that can carry 6 to 8 people. There will be handles on both sides for you to hold on to to avoid falling off. You will also be wearing life jackets that will keep you afloat in case you fall in the water. Exhilarate in a bouncy ride as a speed boat passes your boat, causing turmoil in the water. A thrilling activity that you indulge in at Banana Beach is underwater Sea Walking. You will need to get yourself trained before you can embark on this unique adventure activity.

There are no deck chairs and umbrellas but you shelter from the sun only under the trees. Lots of longtails that take you from the larger nearby beaches like surin and Kamala. Two restaurants on opposite sides with Thai food and more expensive prices than usual. A day here is really recommended

reviews.title: Wonderful guided experience to Banana Beach
reviews.text: Had fun on the day drip to Banana Beach.... Of you are looking for a more 'chill' option over the crowds of Phi Phi, this could be a good choice for you.  We opted for a massage and snorkeling with our package, but other options include parasailing, sea walking, and banana boat (sadly, it was too windy for the boats, but there were a few parasailing slots later in the day when the dind died down).Negatives: The food (buffet included in the tour package) was mediocre (but it's a tiny island and there is only really 1 option). Also during the snorkeling excursion we were surprisingly swarmed by jellyfish( not a problem from the tour operation, just bad luck) but the staff took care of the stings and had vinegar on hand.  Just be mindful if they are close by, as the tide can change and bring them in. Trust me, they definitely sting!  Overall I'd totally recommend this to anyone for a quick 15 min ride from RaoWai.  It feels like a 100 km away, even though you are close by.

reviews.title: Nope. Not worth it.
reviews.text: We booked a "Half-day" trip to Banana Beach through our hotel (one of the Wyndham collection).  It was billed as "TUI Destination Experiences." It included pick-up and drop-off at the hotel, lunch buffet, and a speedboat to Banana Beach. We chose a package that included snorkeling in two places and use of a clear kayak. We were to return at 2:00 PM.Once we had booked and paid, the "half-day" tour suddenly became longer than any full-day tours we booked the entire time in Thailand. We were picked up from our hotel at 6:30 AM, and picked up a few other participants at other hotels on the way to the pier.  We were first to be picked up but last dropped off--we did not get back to our hotel until 3:50 PM.  Once at the pier, we waited well over an hour for the boat out to the beach.  We were still sitting on the beach waiting for a boat back when the 2:00 PM return time came and went. Once at Banana Beach, all boats use the single, very long "floating pier." That means that the pier moves violently with the waves, and the water was very choppy.  Walking down the pier was like being on an obstacle course TV show.  It was extremely unsafe.  Even one of the staff working on the pier fell. The beach itself is nice until you take the crowds into consideration.  It ended up being unpleasant, and we just wanted to go back to our hotel.Due to the sea conditions (solely due to light winds), the snorkeling was delayed ("wait until we make a decision at this time," then "wait until we make a decision at this next time") and we were eventually taken to one snorkeling spot, not two. The snorkeling itself was great.  The rest of the trip was not.  The beach was immediately unpleasant, even early in the day, because the tour company allowed clearly intoxicated people on the trip and never addressed their behavior.  They were yelling, playing loud music, and taking video of themselves and everyone else to post to a YouTube channel.  Our group was told we had to stay within one small area of beach chairs, so we were trapped with the drunk/high partiers.  The rest of the beach became quite crowded as the morning went on. Some people decided to use the kayaks, which were offered very late in the day for about 20 minutes of use, and the rest of us were forced to wait for them to finish paddling around a very small and crowded area just off the beach.  We were effectively held hostage.  People who had arrived on other tours were waiting as well, since they were apparently in similar situations.  All of us were unhappy with our "tours." The entirety of Banana Beach seems to be run by one company.  Do not book a group tour of this island/beach if you have anything else planned for that day.  There is no guarantee that you will be returned to the pier in time to catch a flight or even a dinner reservation.  If a bit of a windy but very sunny day causes this much chaos, we cannot imagine what would happen if it rained.  People book tours with set start and end times in mind.  Companies should not be allowed to hold people hostage on an island past the set departure time.

reviews.text: Introduction: very kind and organized staff.We spent a whole day at this beach. The structure they created is wonderful, bars, restaurants, bathrooms, shops all built with an eye to the environment respecting the Florida nature that exists in this place. reviews.text: Been here yesterday, we have taken the the Program B (Half Day with 1 Activity Included). When we arrived to the check in area, we got a warm Welcome by the Staffs especially Lily. They are providing light breakfast, some breads, fruits, coffee & tea, etc.. We got introduced by the program and explained what we are going to do. We departed at 10am, took a speedboat and reached Banana Beach for 15minutes.Banana Beach is a small island, with clear sea water, white sand, tall trees, it was overall clean. Staffs were excellent in maintaining it clean and of course the service they are providing are beyond magnificent. They also have sun beds which you could use the whole duration of your trip. The company provides different activities such as ZipLine, Banana Boat, Parasailing, Giant Swing, Scuba Diving, Snorkeling, Kayaking (these are all I remember). We originally planned to take the parasailing but due to the strong winds we were unable to do it instead we have done the zip line which has 11 plat forms. After doing the activity, they have served our lunch (fried rice with chicken), also a small bottled water is provided, unlimited!It’s a great place to visit! Hearing the sounds of waves makes you forgot the stressful life in the city.

reviews.title: Banana Beach
reviews.text: Great tour, timetable was planned very efficiently. We booked an all day tour to banana beach in Koh Hey that included a really delicious lunch, snorkeling, and clear bottom kayaking. It was quite crowded on the beach and dining area but not in the ocean. Lots of tourists, but likely due to Lunar New Year holiday for China. The facilities are clean and spaced out. The water is super clear and pristine, lots of areas with coral and fish. The only feedback is probably to have their organization strongly suggest using coral-safe sunblock to the tourists. There was an alarmingly large area of just dead coral on the opposite side of the island where they took us snorkeling.

reviews.title: Gorgeous island with good snorkelling a short boat ride from Phuket
reviews.text: Trips to Banana Beach are either via the tour company that has exclusive tour access, or via a private speed boat / long tail boat. We visited using the tour company, who also included some snorkelling at a nearby bay, banquet lunch at the Hornbill restaurant, tea/coffee with biscuits for afternoon tea, masks and snorkels, and free water/soft-drink during the day. They also ensured that a gluten-free lunch was available. It was a great day, and the swimming and snorkelling was fantastic. Most of the visitors didn't seem to do this, and instead sat on chairs on the beach, so missed out. The best snorkelling on Banana Beach was on the far side of the pontoon jetty, away from the boats, and there was plenty of coral and fish to see. One of our snorkels was broken, but it was easily swapped over at the hire place, although I suspect it was immediately hired out again, so I suggest checking any masks/snorkels as soon as you hire them.

reviews.title: Such a wonderful day. We loved it.
reviews.text: We booked the Banana Beach tour on a whim with our hotel tour desk at the Diamond Cliff Resort, and this was the best decision we've made since arriving here!We originally booked for the next day, however, I fell ill and couldn't make it. Even though there was a no refund policy after acertain period (6pm night before), upon calling the team early morning when we were supposed to go, they were  accommodating and were able to transfer our booking for the following day.The team were fantastic, friendly, informative and could communicate in perfect English. We had a driver in a shuttle that was air-conditioned pick us up at 8:30 am and take us to the pier. Our guides Lily and Boat were fantastic and spoke great English. The speedboat itself was modern and extremely clean. Our first stop was at Racha Yai Island where we were able to swim or relax on the beach, followed by snorkelling in the coral islands and finally r&r at the beautiful Banana Beach for 3 hours, where we could snorkle, swim and kayak. We chose the clear kayak boat (as part of our full day tour) during decent tide on the day (1pm)and it was stunning to be able to see coral and aquatic life in the clear water. We had a delicious banquet for lunch (which on the day included tom yum soup, satay prawns, sweet chilli calamari, papaya salad, fried chicken and tropical fruits).Extremely glad my husband and I booked this tour on a whim. Loved it!
